walkthroughs.body_html:
All probabilities live between 0 and 1.

  • 0 = impossible (e.g. rolling a 7 on a normal dice)
  • 1 = certain (e.g. the sun rising)
  • 0.5 = even chance (e.g. a fair coin landing on heads)

You can write probabilities as fractions, decimals or percentages.

For a fair situation:

P(event) = favourable outcomes ÷ total outcomes

Example: a fair six-sided dice. P(rolling a 4) = 1/6. P(rolling an even number) = 3/6 = 1/2, because there are 3 even outcomes (2, 4, 6) out of 6.

Mutually exclusive events cannot happen together — like "rolling a 2" and "rolling a 5" on one dice.

If you list all possible mutually exclusive outcomes, their probabilities add to 1.

P(A) + P(B) +. = 1

So if P(red) = 0.3 and P(blue) = 0.2, then P(any other colour) = 1 − 0.5 = 0.5.

mcqs.q: What is the probability of an IMPOSSIBLE event?
Two events are mutually exclusive if.
options: They always happen together
They cannot happen at the same time
They are independent
They have the same probability

mcqs.q: Are 'independent events' and 'mutually exclusive events' the same?
options: Yes, but only when the probabilities are equal.
No — independent events do not affect each other's probability; mutually exclusive events cannot both happen.
Yes — both mean the events are unrelated.
1 because the coin has clearly been biased by the previous flips.

mcqs.q: Can a probability ever be greater than 1?
options: Yes, but only when expressed as a percentage.
Yes, but only when the probabilities are equal.
Yes — if an event is very likely, the probability can be 1.5 or 2.
No — probabilities range from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain).

mcqs.q: If you've flipped a fair coin and got heads 5 times in a row, what is the probability the next flip is heads?
options: Less than 1/2, because the coin is 'due' to land on tails to balance the results.
1/2 — each flip is independent of the previous ones.
1 because the coin has clearly been biased by the previous flips.
Yes, but only when expressed as a percentage.
